chunks.arabic_text: عَاشِرًا - أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، الْبَرْقِيُّ، يُكْنَى أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ.

translations.en: 10 – Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, al-Barqī, known by the kunya of Abū Jaʿfar.

chunks.arabic_text: طَعَنَ الْقُمِّيُونَ عَلَيْهِ، وَلَيْسَ الطَّعْنُ فِيهِ، إِنَّمَا الطَّعْنُ فِي مَنْ يَرْوِي عَنْهُ؛ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُبَالِي عَمَّنْ يَأْخُذُ، عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ أَهْلِ الْأَخْبَارِ. وَكَانَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى أَبْعَدَهُ عَنْ قُمٍّ، ثُمَّ أَعَادَهُ إِلَيْهَا وَاعْتَذَرَ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: The Qummis spoke against him, but the defamation is not about him. The defamation was only with regards to whom he narrated from, for he was not mindful of whom he took from, upon the manner of the people of reports (ahl al-akhbār). Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā banished him from Qum, but he brought him back later and apologized to him.

en.summary: This entry highlights Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, a key figure in the transmission of hadith, noting that the criticism (ṭaʿn) from the Qummī scholars focused not on his personal reliability but on his indiscriminate methodology of accepting narrations, typical of the Ahl al-Akhbār school. The text further records a specific historical incident where Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā initially exiled him from Qum for this practice but later recalled him after he offered an apology, illustrating the nuanced approach to scholarly correction in early Shia circles.
en.seo_question: Who is Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi and what was the nature of the criticism against him?

key_terms.الْبَرْقِيُّ: Al-Barqī, a nisba indicating origin or association with Barq (a region in Khurasan).
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْأَخْبَارِ: Ahl al-Akhbār, a school of thought emphasizing hadith over reason.
key_terms.الْقُمِّيُونَ: The people of Qum, referring to the scholars or community of that city.
